sections.history: Idumbavanam lies in the Thiruthuraipoondi taluk of Tiruvarur district, in the southern reaches of the Kaveri delta, about 18 km from Thiruthuraipoondi. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. The presiding Shiva is known as Sarguna Nathar and also as Idumbavaneswarar, and the stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian temple of the lower delta, the shrine enshrines Sarguna Nathar in the sanctum, with the goddess Mangalavalli — also Mangalanayaki — in her own shrine, a Nandi, the parivara devatas and the sacred tank in which the demon Idumban is said to have bathed. The temple keeps the quiet plan of a village sanctuary of some antiquity.
sections.legends: The place takes its name from Idumban, a demon who came here burdened with sin, bathed in the temple tank, and worshipped Shiva with devotion. Pleased with his worship, the lord granted him total salvation — and so the forest-place is called Idumbavanam, 'the grove of Idumban.' The lord's name Sarguna Nathar, 'lord of all good qualities,' marks the grace by which even a demon was raised to liberation.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail of the southern delta include Idumbavanam among their stops.
sections.experience: At Idumbavanam the pilgrim comes to a shrine of redeeming grace, where even a demon was granted salvation by his worship. Before Sarguna Nathar and Mangalavalli, beside the tank of Idumban's cleansing, the visitor finds the deep mercy of a Tevaram temple of the southern Kaveri country.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Idumbavanam is in the Thiruthuraipoondi taluk of Tiruvarur district (PIN 614703), about 18 km from Thiruthuraipoondi in the southern delta. Thiruthuraipoondi is the nearest rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
